entities.name: Nalanda University
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary: One of the world's oldest residential universities, active from the 5th century to 1193 CE in Bihar, India. At its height, Nalanda housed 10,000 students and 2,000 teachers studying Buddhist philosophy, logic, grammar, medicine, and astronomy. The great library (Dharmagañja) reportedly burned for months when Bakhtiyar Khilji's forces destroyed the university in 1193.
